problem_statement: nuxt-ui-templates/docs is a Nuxt 4 documentation template built with Nuxt UI and Nuxt Content: a shared app shell (a sticky AppHeader with a logo, a template menu and a primary top-nav where every rendered nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class, plus a shared AppFooter) wraps every page, and docs pages render through the shared documentation layout. On top of the existing Rollout Journey page at /journey (authored as Nuxt Content markdown from the shared MDC section-heading and ::card-group / ::card pattern and registered in the shared top-nav), the docs team now wants a consistent, on-brand ON-PAGE reading aid rendered from the shared app shell across the docs surfaces: (1) a shared 'On this page' section navigator at the head of the content that lists the current page's section headings as green jump chips with the current section clearly highlighted, appearing identically on the Overview (home), the Journey page AND the Getting Started guide; and (2) a release-channel picker with a live readout that names which channel the reader is on (Stable / Edge / LTS). Ship it so the section navigator (a) appears on the Overview, Journey AND Getting Started pages alike (a single shared component, not a per-page copy), (b) lays out its jump-chip row responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (tolerance 24px), (c) matches the Nuxt green/emerald docs styling (a light-green panel, green chips, a readable dark-on-green highlighted current section) rather than an off-palette dark slab or a broken low-contrast card whose active item disappears and whose label collides with the chips, and (d) keeps the channel readout in sync with the picker so a reader who switches to the Edge channel sees the readout update to 'Reading: Edge release channel'. Keep the Journey page, the Home overview, the shared chrome and the Getting Started guide free of horizontal overflow, preserve the existing pages, and keep the runtime clean (no console errors or failed requests). Do not diverge into an off-system one-off, and do not let the navigator go missing on the guide pages or the channel readout go stale after a switch.
required_content: Keep the Rollout Journey page at /journey authored as Nuxt Content markdown through the shared documentation layout and shared app shell, with its 'Journey' entry registered in the shared top-nav so the nav-link renders consistently on the Home page and the Journey page.

Add a shared 'On this page' section navigator at the head of the docs content, rendered from the shared app shell, so it appears on the Overview (home /), the Journey page (/journey) AND the Getting Started guide (/getting-started) alike (a single shared component, not per-page copies).

The navigator shows an 'On this page' label and a row of jump chips naming the current page's sections, with the current section clearly highlighted; its jump-chip row must wrap responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (tolerance 24px).

Style the navigator in the Nuxt docs green/emerald language (a light-green panel, green chips, a readable dark-on-green highlighted current section), not an off-palette dark-slate slab or a low-contrast broken card.

Add a release-channel picker in the shared app shell with a readout, and wire it so that after clicking the Edge chip the readout reads 'Reading: Edge release channel' - it must re-read the live selection, not show a stale captured value.
Keep the existing pages intact and the runtime free of console errors and failed requests.
design_constraints: Implement the section navigator as a single shared component rendered from the shared app shell so one source of truth reaches every docs surface (home, Journey and Getting Started); do not paste divergent per-page copies or build a detached off-system widget.
The jump-chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The navigator must adopt the Nuxt docs theme (the green #00DC82 / emerald accent, a light-green panel background, green chips, an uppercase small-caps label) and the highlighted current section must stay clearly legible (readable dark-on-green), not a foreign dark-slate slab or a low-contrast pale-on-pale card whose active item disappears or whose label collides with the chips.

Place the channel-picker readout in the shared app shell, separate from the navigator, and make it reflect the CURRENT selection after every click by reading the live selected channel, so it can never go stale relative to the highlighted chip.
Preserve the shared app shell, the shared top-nav (including the registered Journey link), the shared section-heading / card scale and the existing docs copy, and do not introduce off-system styling.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home and mobile_home protect the Home overview and the shared chrome across viewports and confirm the Journey nav-link renders in the shared top-nav.
desktop_journey and mobile_journey protect the Rollout Journey page rendered through the shared docs layout, and must carry the shared 'On this page' section navigator at the content head.
desktop_getting_started protects the Getting Started guide and must carry the shared section navigator, proving cross-page consistency.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home bring the section navigator into view and must show the green/emerald navigator with a legible highlighted section and without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_journey protects the navigator's presence on the Journey page.
channel_toggle_home clicks the Edge chip in the channel picker; the readout must then read 'Reading: Edge release channel'.

change_completion: The 'On this page' section navigator is present at the head of the Overview (home), the Journey page AND the Getting Started guide (the shared component reaches all three docs surfaces).

After clicking the Edge chip in the channel picker on the Home page, the readout updates to 'Reading: Edge release channel' - the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Reading: Stable release channel'.
design_consistency: The navigator on the rail states matches the reference's green/emerald docs styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel / ssim / block-fidelity), not an off-palette slab or a broken low-contrast card.

The navigator adopts the Nuxt green theme tokens and light-panel idiom and keeps its highlighted current section legible, so it reads as part of the shared docs design system across every page alongside the registered Journey nav-link.
responsive: No captured docs page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the jump-chip row wraps.
desktop_rail_home, mobile_rail_home and desktop_rail_journey keep the section navigator readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The existing Home overview, the Journey page and the Getting Started guide remain intact with the shared AppHeader top-nav (including the Journey nav-link) and AppFooter chrome.
No content is removed from the existing pages and the Nuxt build stays clean with no console or network errors.

author_notes: L4 hardening of the nuxt-ui-templates/docs Nuxt 4 (Nuxt UI + Nuxt Content) documentation template. The original L2 task added a Rollout Journey page at /journey (Nuxt Content markdown, shared MDC ::card-group / ::card layout, registered 'Journey' entry in the shared top-nav); that add is preserved as identical INFRA across all legs. The L4 lever is a NATIVE docs feature: a shared 'On this page' section navigator rendered from the app shell at the head of the docs content, listing the current page's section headings as green jump chips - the kind of on-page nav a real docs framework ships - plus a release-channel picker readout in the shared shell. INFRA (identical across reference, baseline, bad): remote content fonts are vendored locally at build time so the site serves fully offline; nuxt.config autoSubfolderIndex is set so guide routes resolve as directories; the shared AppHeader/AppFooter chrome, the Journey page markdown, the app.config Journey nav entry and the nav-link class are byte-identical across legs. The four orthogonal levers ride on the shared navigator plus the channel-picker readout host. reference = navigator on the Home, Journey AND Getting Started pages, fluid wrap, green/emerald styling with a legible highlighted section, and a channel readout that re-reads the live selection (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = an unrepaired navigator present on the Home page only (fails D2 cross-page on the Journey + Getting Started surfaces), a fixed 780px nowrap jump-chip track (fails D6 mobile overflow), an off-brand dark-slate palette (fails D3), but its channel readout IS synced on click (passes D4, leg-orthogonal). bad = a genuinely broken navigator present on the Home page only (fails D2), a 560px nowrap track + a shallow inner overflow-x:hidden non-fix (fails D6), a near-invisible pale-mint-on-pale-mint highlighted section with the label collapsed onto and overlapping the chip row (fails D3), and a channel readout wired from a value snapshotted once at setup so it stays 'Stable' after switching to Edge (fails D4) - bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The Nuxt generate build renders every page with self-hosted fonts and no network calls.
